handback.t:
H22 is finished. Verdict: the MLP router is not kept. The cascade-style net wins in more than one real-shaped world, but it is not harmless in the keyword worlds or the no-information control, so it is at most an opt-in linear embedding head.

All numbers are simulated: the text, tokens and MiniLM embeddings are real, but every competence function, keyword prior and outcome is mine. I used no FANN, no crates and no downloads, and made no src edits.

**Protocol.** I tuned on seeds 1-8, evaluated on held 31-60, and ran the same frozen configs on confirm 61-90. Stats are paired 95% CI plus Holm, with TOST ±0.01 reported alongside. Best fair baseline means the best of 16 baseline arms: the 6 requested routers, each with plain tokens, with tokens plus 32-anchor tokens, and with tokens plus 128-anchor tokens (offline k-means, standing in for the repo's knowledge-anchor feature). The best was picked per world and volume on the evaluated seeds.

**g12 reproduction.** All 120 cells × 8 arms (6 baselines, `ann`, `ann+kw`) match `results/g12_annrouter*.json` exactly (max diff 0) in both splits.

**Existing keyword worlds (sim ×3, f3 big/BigTail, T=2000/6000/20000).**
- g12 `ann` loses everywhere, by -0.02 to -0.19.
- The new cascade net (`casc`) tuned on seeds 1-8 still loses, but by much less: -0.020..-0.035 at T=2000, -0.001..-0.024 at 6000, +0.003..-0.015 at 20000.
- Only about 4 of 30 cells pass TOST ±0.01.
- Tasks-to-parity for `casc` against the late-best baseline is unstable: 500 in held versus 10500 in confirm for sim-fixed/random, 11.5-15.5k for no-traps, 18.5k or never for big.
- `ann` never reaches parity.

**Real-shaped worlds.** There are 12 worlds, two text sources (A with 9240 sentences, B with 5307) × six kinds:
- clu12-6ag and clu48-32ag: competence is a table over k-means clusters of the sentence embedding.
- smlin-6ag: smooth linear function of random projections of the embedding.
- smrbf-8ag and smrbf-drift-8ag: smooth RBF skill, with the centres shifted at T/2 in the drift variant.
- control: shuffled competence, so no information anywhere.

The 1-hidden-layer MLP (`mlp(emb)`, real 384-d embedding as input):
- It loses by Holm in 9-10 of 12 worlds at T=2000 and 6000, down to -0.13 in clu48 and -0.08 in smrbf.
- At T=20000 it is roughly at parity in clu12 (-0.003/-0.012). It wins only in the drift worlds (+0.008/+0.012 held, +0.011/+0.010 confirm).
- Against the best anchor-Hebbian baseline specifically the picture is the same, except smrbf ties.
- Without the embedding it is much worse (clu12 .558 vs .678 at 20000), so the embedding does help it. But the anchor-feature Hebbian router uses that information as well as the MLP does.

The cascade-correlation-style growing net (`casc(emb)`):
- It loses or ties at T=2000.
- At T=6000 it wins in two worlds in both splits: A-smlin (+0.013 held, +0.011 confirm) and A-smrbf-drift (+0.006, +0.010).
- At T=20000 it wins in 6 of 12 worlds in both splits: clu12 (+0.015 on A and B), smlin (+0.035/+0.024), drift (+0.016/+0.017). Against the anchor-Hebbian baseline it also wins smrbf (+0.009/+0.007).
- It loses clu48-32ag (-0.03..-0.05) and smrbf against the plain keyword prior (-0.02..-0.026).
- It loses to the shuffled control by -0.007..-0.009 at 20000.
- Full-stream crossover is between 2000 and 6000 tasks. In the 20000-task curves it reaches parity at 500-1500 tasks in clu12/smlin/drift, 3500-5000 versus anchor-Hebbian in smrbf, 17k in B-clu48, and never in A-clu48.

The gain comes from the linear head, not the hidden units. The cascade net's stage-0 reference (hmax 0, a per-agent logistic head on the embedding plus the keyword skip) beats the grown cascade, which beats the MLP. For example A-clu12 at T=20000: .7076 vs .6960 vs .6779, with the same ordering in all 10 informative worlds in both splits. I did not pre-declare a test for this, so it is a read from the numbers, not a Holm result.

**Keep rule.**
- The MLP is not kept. It wins in one family only, and `ann` loses the keyword worlds by up to -0.19.
- The cascade net technically wins in more than one real-shaped world, but it is not harmless. It loses the keyword worlds by -0.004..-0.035, loses the control at 20000, and fails the 32-agent and RBF worlds. The only defensible form is an opt-in linear head on embeddings, for pools of at most 8 agents and at least 6000 tasks that already compute embeddings. No src patch proposed.

**Cost (single thread, noisy ±30%; 6-agent / 32-agent worlds).**

| Router | ns/decision | State |
|---|---|---|
| keyword | 293 / 167 | |
| f64 recommended router | 3.5k / 7.4k | 987 / 2499 kB |
| CompactRouter | 1.4k / 2.2k | 87 / 136 kB owned |
| MLP pca16 H16 | 0.8k / 1.4k | 34 kB |
| MLP raw384 H48 with replay | 19k / 21k | 226 kB |
| `casc` raw384, linear head | 4.8k / 23k | |
| `casc` raw384, 6 hidden + replay | 26k / 72k | 71 / 164 kB |

Encoding the task text with MiniLM costs 3.3-7.6 ms per query, about 1000× the router decision.

**Caveats.**
- The smooth worlds' keyword prior is informed, which makes the baselines strong early.
- Worlds sample sentences with replacement, so B at 20000 repeats each sentence about 4×.
- Anchors are idealised offline k-means.
- The cascade net was tuned over 96 configs against 28 per baseline variant.
- smlin is linear in random projections by construction.
- One `cargo build` was accidentally run into `nm-target-r2`, which is not my target dir. Everything else used `nm-target-r1`.
